title: How to talk about the Beneve opportunity
titleHtml: How to talk about the Beneve opportunity
sub: For anyone asking what you actually do, however they got to the question.

tracks.label: They asked what you do
tracks.hint: The best version of this conversation. They opened it, so do not oversell the answer.

steps.title: Answer in two sentences
steps.lead: Long answers sound like a pitch. Short ones sound like a job:
script: I share wellness products I actually use, and I get paid a share of what sells. Beneve puts 65% of every dollar into compensation, which is why it is worth doing properly.
There are thirteen ways to earn in the plan, but honestly most people start with one and add later.

steps.title: Send the page, not a pitch
steps.lead: Let them read it alone. People decide about money in private:
script: Easier to read it than have me describe it: [your Beneve opportunity link]
Have a look whenever, and ask me the awkward questions after. I would rather you ask them than not join because nobody did.
steps.copyLabel: Copy the send the page text

tracks.label: They think it is an MLM pitch
tracks.hint: You will get this. Answering it straight is the only thing that works.

steps.title: Do not dodge the question
steps.lead: Denying the category loses the room. Name what is actually different:
script: Fair question, and yes it is a referral model. What is different here is written down: 65% of every dollar allocated to compensation, and an Influencer Bill of Rights that says the company cannot touch your social channels or your audience.
You can read both before you talk to me again if you want.
steps.copyLabel: Copy the straight answer to the MLM question

steps.title: Give them the exit
steps.lead: Offering an easy no is what makes a yes believable:
script: If it is not for you that is genuinely fine, and I am not going to keep messaging you about it.
You are welcome to just use the products, plenty of people do.

tip: Tip: Never quote an income figure, promise a result, or describe this as passive. Say what the plan pays and let people do their own arithmetic. Compliance aside, the people who join off a hyped number are the ones who quit first.
